project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 296 (System blocks promotion when no clean sequestered epoch remains, which returns a terminal state rather than reusing a retired epoch)
project_specification.addition_summary:
Implement app_spec.xml feature 296 in the existing promotion member (packages/promotion, import name promotion; seat src/app/modules/promotion): a *terminal-state verdict*, `blocks_when_no_clean_epoch_remains(epochs, *, budget=SEQUESTERED_EPOCH_BUDGET)` (and a `PromotionBlockedError` error class opening the greppable code `no_clean_epoch_remains`), that judges the whole epoch ledger and refuses promotion when every sequestered epoch has served §13 item 4's budget of three promotion decisions. This is the second sentence of docs/alpha-engine-prd.md §13 item 4, quoted whole because both of its sentences are this feature's brief:
Sequestered epochs are retired permanently after **3 promotion decisions**. Track in a ledger. When clean epochs run out, the system stops. That is a legitimate terminal state.
Feature 295 is the first sentence's threshold — it refuses one epoch once that epoch has served its budget; feature 296 is the second sentence's verdict — it declares the terminal state only when *every* epoch has. The two are deliberately **not** one thing: 295 answers *may this epoch still be spent?* about one row, while 296 answers *may the system continue at all?* about the whole table, and the answer to the second is not the conjunction of the firsts — an operator told "epoch X is spent" when the truth is "every epoch is spent, so promotion stops" would go looking for a clean epoch that does not exist. So feature 296 adds its own error class and its own code, in the same member, as a sibling of feature 295's `EpochSelectionError` under the same `PromotionError` base — not a new member, not a new component, not a new table. The footprint is two production files and their test: one new module (`packages/promotion/src/promotion/terminal.py`) plus one edit to the member's existing error vocabulary and its `__init__.py` re-export. The verdict is a *judgment over the whole ledger the caller already reads*: it takes the ledger's rows (duck-read as `epoch_id` and `promotion_decisions_served`, so the composed listing and a test's stand-ins judge identically) and either the system may continue or it may not. It is deliberately **not** a route: feature 291's `POST /promotion/pre-register` is the category's one exposure, and a second endpoint that only refuses would be a second door to the same table with none of the booking's obligations attached — the verdict is reached through the seat (src/app/modules/promotion) the same way features 295 and 297 reach the ledger. No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration is edited; no new `@register` component is added (the promotion member's single `"promotion"` component, feature 291's registry store, is untouched); the member joins by workspace-scan convention and does not import another workspace member.

category.name: Promotion & Epoch Governance
category.feature: System blocks promotion when no clean sequestered epoch remains, which returns a terminal state rather than reusing a retired epoch.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (packages/* members, import names are underscored slugs) / pytest (ruff + mypy conventions). The module loader (src/app/module_loader.py) discovers members from the root pyproject.toml `[tool.uv.workspace] members = ["packages/*"]`, imports each package so its module-level `@register` fires, and composes what each `@register` builder contributes under a component name. `app` (src/app) is a namespace package with no `__init__.py`; the seats in src/app/modules/<member>/ are reached by namespace import (e.g. app.modules.promotion). A member never imports another member — it reaches shared shapes through `app.*`, never through a sibling package's import name.
existing_context.test_baseline: The repository-level suite under tests/ is collected by pytest with testpaths=tests; each workspace member's own suite lives under packages/<member>/tests/ and is collected under its own conftest (same-basename files collide under one pytest run), and is NOT graded by the bare `uv run pytest` acceptance gate — a member suite must be run explicitly (run both `uv run pytest tests/` and the member's own `packages/promotion/tests/`). Feature 296 is a pure judgment over ledger rows the caller already holds, so it adds no third-party dependency: it is a comparison over each row's served count against §13 item 4's budget of three. Measure the real numbers by running the suite before relying on them. The repo lint is red on main (mypy absent, pre-existing ruff errors), so lint only the changed files and compare to a sibling.
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, frozen dataclasses for value types, docstrings that cite app_spec.xml feature numbers and docs/alpha-engine-prd.md / migrations/versions/0110_epoch_ledger.py by path, errors split by the repair the caller must make, no member imports another, the set is the tables an act's own statements name.
existing_context.dependencies: Feature 291 (pre-registration, the registry row), feature 293 (the decision stamp), feature 294 (the epoch charge, whose `epoch`/`epochs` read this verdict is a function of), feature 295 (the selection gate, whose per-epoch budget this verdict is deliberately not), feature 300 (the forward window, which reaches the same ledger). depends_on: 296 on 295.

project_specification.constraints: - Feature 296 is a *whole-table verdict*, not a per-epoch one: it answers *may the system continue?* by judging whether every sequestered epoch has served §13 item 4's budget, and it is the second sentence of §13 item 4, not the first. Feature 295's `rejects_further_selection` answers the first sentence about one epoch (`served >= budget`); feature 296 answers the second about the whole ledger (`every row served >= budget`). The two are separate modules and separate error classes, because they answer different questions with different repairs — 295's repair is *select a clean epoch*, 296's is *stop, the terminal state §13 item 4 calls legitimate*. - The verdict takes the ledger's rows as a single argument — the whole-table read feature 294's `epochs()` seam answers with — and judges them: it is the read plus the comparison, and the comparison is pure and spelled on its own as `blocks_when_no_clean_epoch_remains(rows, *, budget=SEQUESTERED_EPOCH_BUDGET)`, the split feature 295's `rejects_further_selection` and `EpochSelections.select` state for the selection gate. The rows are duck-read (`epoch_id` and `promotion_decisions_served`), so the composed listing and a test's stand-ins judge identically. - The verdict is *derived from the ledger*, not a persisted fact: it writes nothing, spells no DDL, authors no statement, opens no connection, and gains no fifth order in `promotion.schema` — the `retired` flag is the exhaustion machinery's persistence of the verdict, and this verdict is the judgment that precedes it, not a second spelling of it. It must not read the `retired` flag to decide (that would be 296's own reader reading itself — a circularity the terminal state is built to avoid), must not read `sealed_at` (the sealing process's fact, which judges nothing here), and must not read a pool, a score, a coverage ledger, a calibration status or any promotion merit (whether the promotion *stands* is the deciding evaluation's verdict, feature 292's mismatch is the only comparison against the recorded hash, and features 298's and 299's refusals read the campaign and the coverage ledger — tables this act never opens). It must not spell feature 292's `criteria_mismatch` verdict. - The budget is §13 item 4's own number, **three**, spelled once in feature 295's `SEQUESTERED_EPOCH_BUDGET` and *used* here, not restated — a second spelling of `3` would be a second place the budget lives, free to disagree with the one the selection gate compares against. The comparison is `>=`, the spelling migrations/versions/0110_epoch_ledger.py's docstring gives feature 295 (`promotion_decisions_served >= 3`), so an epoch that has *exceeded* its budget counts as spent on the same comparison rather than falling through an equality pin. The `budget` keyword defaults to that one value and is not re-spelled. - The verdict is **not** the conjunction of feature 295's per-epoch refusals, and a test must catch the difference: when every epoch is spent the verdict refuses with `no_clean_epoch_remains` and names the whole ledger, but when one epoch is spent and another is clean it does **not** refuse — it answers that the system may continue (the clean epoch), leaving the per-epoch refusal to feature 295's gate at the moment that spent epoch is selected. The verdict is a question about the *system's* continuation, not about any one epoch's spend. - An **empty ledger** — no sequestered epoch at all — is refused as a distinct, terminal fact, not read as "zero spent, all clean": there is no epoch to spend, so promotion has nothing to run on, and the verdict refuses with `no_clean_epoch_remains` naming the absence. This keeps feature 295's two answers apart (an absent row is *nobody sealed it*, not a clean epoch) at the whole-table level: a ledger with no rows is not a ledger full of clean epochs, and reading it as "all clean" would let a deployment that never sequestered an epoch book a promotion against nothing. The refusal names the sealing process's act as the repair. - The verdict raises `PromotionBlockedError` (opening the greppable code `no_clean_epoch_remains`) when the system may not continue — every epoch spent, or the ledger empty — and answers that the system may continue (returning the count of clean epochs remaining, so the caller that wants to log or carry it does not read the table a second time, and so feature 297's depleting count and this verdict agree on the figure) otherwise. Raising rather than answering a boolean is the stance feature 295's `rejects_further_selection` takes: the verdict is the last line before the system stops, so the stop has to be the function's own act rather than a branch every caller must remember to make. - `PromotionBlockedError` is a **sibling** of feature 295's `EpochSelectionError` under `PromotionError`, not a face of it, not a face of feature 294's `EpochChargeError`, and not a face of feature 293's `PromotionDecisionError`: it is deliberately none of them, because its noun is different — not *a count did not land* (294), not *a stamp did not land* (293), not *one epoch's budget is spent* (295), but *every epoch is spent, so promotion is blocked and the system stops*. An operator who greps `epoch_budget_spent` for this refusal would be looking for one spent epoch when the finding is that all of them are; an operator who greps `epoch_charge_unpersisted` would be debugging a write that succeeded. So feature 296 adds its own code, `no_clean_epoch_remains`, distinct from 295's `epoch_budget_spent` and 294's `epoch_charge_unpersisted` on their shared `epoch_`/`epoch_charge_` domain prefix. - Its faces stay **gathered** in one class, the argument every gathered class in `promotion.errors` makes: this feature's caller is a gate, and a gate's one failure mode is silence. A caller whose single `except PromotionBlockedError` guards its promotion path must not be able to walk through a hole because a malformed ask arrived in a different class from the terminal state — in every case promotion is blocked and the caller must not proceed. So the ask (a served count that is not a count) and the verdict (every epoch spent, or the ledger empty) all open with `no_clean_epoch_remains` and all name what they are about. This is the same caller-position override the gathered classes before it state, one member over. - The verdict holds no cache of counts this process had already judged, for the reason every store in this member states for its rows: the ledger is the only record of what the epochs have served, so it is the only thing a verdict is drawn from, judged on every call, in every process — a charge lands in another process a moment after this one asked, and the epoch that was clean is spent. - No component, no seat, no router, no second builder. The member's registered surface stays feature 291's one store, for the reason every sibling states: a builder takes no arguments and is built on every `create_app()` call, while *whether every epoch is spent* is a fact about rows that move and no composition can supply it. The verdict is constructed from the charge store by the caller that has one (or from a URL through the module-level spelling), and the seat (src/app/modules/promotion) is untouched — it must still export exactly `{"COMPONENT_NAME", "promotion_registry_component"}` and must not re-export the terminal vocabulary, the same discipline feature 295's seat test pins for the selection vocabulary. - Stdlib only, and import-cheap: `os`, `collections.abc` and `typing` at module scope plus this member's own modules (`epoch` for the budget and the `epochs` seam, `errors` for the shared base) — not even `sqlite3`, because the connection is the charge store's and this module never opens one — so the factory's scan imports this package for the near-nothing it always did. - All existing tests in the promotion member (packages/promotion/tests) and in tests/ must stay green. The member's own suite must be run explicitly (it is not graded by the bare gate). - Do not edit the order-sensitive shared files: src/app/middleware.py, src/app/settings.py, migrations/versions/**, alembic/versions/**.

implementation_steps.step: Phase 1 — the error class and the code. Add a `NO_CLEAN_EPOCH_REMAINS_CODE = "no_clean_epoch_remains"` constant and a `PromotionBlockedError(PromotionError)` error class to the member's existing error vocabulary (`packages/promotion/src/promotion/errors.py`) as the ninth top-level sibling of feature 295's `EpochSelectionError`, under the same `PromotionError` base. Its noun is the exhausted holdout resource itself — every sequestered epoch has served §13 item 4's budget, so promotion is blocked and the system stops, the terminal state §13 item 4 explicitly legitimates — and its repair is unlike any of the eight beside it: not *re-send the ask* (the ask may be well formed), not *fix the deployment* (nothing failed to write — every count is on its row), not *grow coverage or re-plan a campaign* (those are features 298's and 299's merit findings about the pool and the campaign), not *restore a record* (293) or *re-persist a count* (294), and not *select a clean epoch* (295) — because there is no clean epoch left to select. The repair is to stop, the terminal state §13 item 4 calls legitimate. It is deliberately **not** a face of feature 295's `EpochSelectionError`: that class reports *one epoch's budget is spent*, with a repair of *select a clean epoch*; this one reports *every epoch is spent*, with no clean epoch left to select — conflating them would send an operator looking for a clean epoch that does not exist. Every message opens with `no_clean_epoch_remains` and names the exhausted ledger. Update the module docstring of `errors.py` to place the new class in the tree (the "tree is open" paragraph already names 296 as a seam that lands on this module), and add the class and code to `__all__`.

Phase 2 — the verdict. Add one new module, `packages/promotion/src/promotion/terminal.py`: the whole-table verdict. (1) `blocks_when_no_clean_epoch_remains(rows, *, budget=SEQUESTERED_EPOCH_BUDGET)`: the pure half of the pair — the feature's whole sentence as one comparison, and the seam for the caller that **already holds the figure**. It validates each row's served count (a non-negative integer, `bool` refused first — `True` is `1` and a flag where a count belongs would silently answer one decision nobody recorded; negative refused, because no honest count of rows is negative and no writer in this member could have landed one) and judges whether every sequestered epoch has served `budget` (`served >= budget`, the spelling 0110's own docstring gives feature 295): when every epoch has, or the ledger is empty, it raises `PromotionBlockedError` (message opening with `no_clean_epoch_remains`, stating how many epochs were judged, how many were spent, the terminal state §13 item 4 calls legitimate, and the repair — stop, there is no clean epoch to select); otherwise it returns the count of clean epochs remaining (the figure feature 297's depleting count reports and this verdict agrees with, so the caller that wants to log or carry it does not read the table a second time). The rows are duck-read (`epoch_id` and `promotion_decisions_served`), so the composed listing and a test's stand-ins judge identically. It takes no `clock`, no `node_id`, and reads neither `retired` nor `sealed_at`. (2) A `TerminalStates` gate class constructed **over** an `EpochCharges` (or anything with its `epochs` seam — the whole-table read feature 294 adds), duck-typed rather than `isinstance`-guarded for the reason `EpochSelections` states: the factory's scan imports this member under a synthetic module name, so the composed store and the directly imported one are different class objects with the same seam. Its `blocks()` method performs the whole-table read through the seam and delegates to the pure judgment, so there is one comparison in the member and this act cannot disagree with the pure judgment a caller may use directly. It holds no cache, owns no connection, runs no bootstrap, authors no DDL and spells no statement — the one table the read needs is brought up by the charge store's own connect, and `promotion.schema` gains no fifth order because the set a bootstrap runs is the set an act's own statements name and this act's statements name nothing at all. It is `from_env`-constructible, returning `None` when nothing names a relational store. (3) A module-level `block_when_no_clean_epoch_remains(epoch_id_unused_or_rows, *, database_url=None, env=None)` spelling that resolves the charge store from `database_url`, else `DATABASE_URL`, exactly as `select_epoch` resolves its gate, and performs the whole-table read then delegates — the feature's sentence as one call for the caller that wants the verdict without holding stores. A `PromotionBlockedError` from the judgment propagates unwrapped.

Phase 3 — the whole-table read on the charge store. Add an `epochs()` method to `EpochCharges` in `packages/promotion/src/promotion/epoch.py` — the whole-table listing this verdict reads through, the mirror of feature 293's `decisions()` listing. It reads every `epoch_ledger` row (the four columns, validated, with the doubled-row case unreachable through the owner's DDL and refused anyway — a second row for one epoch would split its served count and let the verdict read a spent epoch as clean), ordered by the table's key so two reads of one store are comparable, and returns them as `ServingEpoch` values. It is the read the verdict is a function of, and it is added to the charge store rather than spelled here, so the count this verdict judges and the counts the charge answered with cannot be two readings of one table — the discipline `promotion.epoch` states for its count and `promotion.selection` states for its gate. Re-export nothing new from `__init__.py` for it (it is reached through the charge store the verdict is constructed over, the same way `decisions()` is reached through the decision store), and add no schema order. Update the module docstring of `epoch.py` to note the listing as a read the exhaustion machinery's whole-table verdict reaches.

Phase 4 — the re-export. Re-export `PromotionBlockedError`, `NO_CLEAN_EPOCH_REMAINS_CODE`, `blocks_when_no_clean_epoch_remains`, `TerminalStates` and `block_when_no_clean_epoch_remains` from the member's existing `__init__.py` (`packages/promotion/src/promotion/__init__.py`) alongside feature 295's existing names, and add them to `__all__`. No new component, no new `@register` builder, no new seat export — the member's single `"promotion"` component (feature 291's registry store) is untouched, and `[name for name in dir(member) if name.startswith("build_")]` must still equal `["build_promotion_registry"]`.

Phase 5 — the tests. Add one test module, `packages/promotion/tests/test_promotion_terminal.py`, asserting: the pure judgment answers the count of clean epochs remaining when at least one epoch is under budget (and does not refuse), and raises `PromotionBlockedError` opening `no_clean_epoch_remains` when every epoch has served the budget — through the real acts of features 291, 293 and 294 rather than a hand-written row (book and decide three promotions against each of two epochs, charge each, then the verdict refuses); an empty ledger is refused as a distinct terminal fact, not read as "all clean"; the verdict does **not** refuse when one epoch is spent and another is clean (the per-epoch refusal is 295's, at selection time) — the difference between a whole-table verdict and the conjunction of per-epoch refusals; the verdict reads the whole ledger through feature 294's `epochs()` seam (pinned: no `FROM epoch_ledger` spelled in the module, the gate drives the `epochs` verb, and `promotion.schema` gains no fifth order — a fresh database gets only the ledger table, created by the charge store's own connect); the verdict judges neither the `retired` flag nor `sealed_at` (pinned on `.retired`, `RETIRED_COLUMN`, `.sealed_at`, `SEALED_AT_COLUMN` absent from the module's code) and reads no merit or evidence (`regime_coverage`, `campaign`, `ir_oos`, `score`, `calibration` absent) and never spells `criteria_mismatch`; the verdict writes nothing (a permitted and a refused verdict leave the raw ledger byte-identical, read before and after on the raw row); the budget is the PRD's own number spelled once (3 in `selection`, absent from `epoch` and `terminal`); the verdict holds no cache (a charge landing behind its back moves the answer); the served count is validated (a `bool`, a negative, a fraction, text refused in the verdict's own vocabulary); `PromotionBlockedError` is a `PromotionError` and a sibling of `EpochSelectionError` (not a subclass of it, of `EpochChargeError`, or of `PromotionDecisionError`), with a distinct code (`no_clean_epoch_remains != epoch_budget_spent != epoch_charge_unpersisted`); every refusal the verdict drives opens with `no_clean_epoch_remains` (the gathered-class argument, one face); the module-level spelling resolves the URL it is handed and the ambient `DATABASE_URL`, and refuses a deployment naming no database by name; `from_env` answers `None` without a database; the vocabulary is reachable from the member's surface; the member still exports exactly one builder; the seat is untouched (`set(seat.__all__) == {"COMPONENT_NAME", "promotion_registry_component"}`, and the seat does not re-export `TerminalStates` or `PromotionBlockedError`); and the spec's sentence is what the module implements (the suite reads `System blocks promotion when no clean sequestered epoch remains, which returns a terminal state rather than reusing a retired epoch` from app_spec.xml).

Phase 6 — verify. Run the promotion member's own suite (`uv run pytest packages/promotion/tests`) and the repository-level suite (`uv run pytest tests/`) — both, since the member suite is not graded by the bare gate — and confirm all pass. Lint only the changed files against a sibling (the repo lint is red on main). Confirm feature 291-295's and 300's behaviour and tests are untouched, that no new component is registered (`scan_components` still reports exactly one `promotion` component), that the member still exports exactly one `build_` builder, that the seat still exports exactly `{"COMPONENT_NAME", "promotion_registry_component"}` and does not re-export the terminal vocabulary, and that no order-sensitive shared file was edited.
